exposure: Repetitive needle prickling (painful stimulation) immediately after birth
outcome: Sensory functions (paw withdrawal with von Frey filaments, calibrated forceps test)
cohort: Male and female Wistar rats were exposed to either painful stimulation or served as controls immediately after birth.
finding: Pain in the neonatal period negatively influences sensory and motor functions during development in male and female rats, even long term after the painful stimulus ceased, with similar responses between sexes.
